_comment: COUPLING tier-2. A SECOND cross-code pair for two-way TSI, so the capability belongs to the coupling path rather than to one pairing that happened to work: NGSolve thermal with FEniCSx structural, and scikit-fem thermal with NGSolve structural. NGSolve is the hard participant on purpose — netgen gives it an UNSTRUCTURED mesh while dolfinx and scikit-fem both use a tensor-product triangulation here, so every exchange in these arrangements maps between a regular grid and an irregular cloud, in both directions, and no node can coincide with a partner node by accident. It is also a different structural discretisation: VectorH1 order 2 with per-component Dirichlet boundaries (dirichletx= / dirichlety=), where a plain dirichlet= would clamp both components and silently turn transverse rollers into a built-in edge. Same battery as the other pair fixtures: convergence, monolithic agreement, interface sensitivity per participant, and the reverse-direction control checked both for size and against the monolithic two-way-minus-one-way difference. A THIRD MUTATION WAS TRIED AND DOES NOT DISCRIMINATE, and it is recorded here rather than dropped: shrinking the STRUCTURAL participant's body to 75% of the thermal one's, so every exchange beyond that point is an extrapolation. It changes nothing measurable. Two reasons, both worth knowing. (a) In uniaxial strain tr(eps) = beta*theta/(lam+2mu) POINTWISE, so the exported strain does not depend on where the body ends and shortening it barely moves the field. (b) `couple`'s interface-identity check is a DISJOINTNESS test — it fires when the two point clouds do not overlap at all, not when one is contained in the other — so a participant solving on a smaller body than its partner is not detected. That is a real gap in the checks and not a defect of this fixture; it is recorded in the coupling pitfall corpus.

_mutation.note: Kill the reverse direction. Both arrangements converge faster and every iteration-level check passes; the monolithic comparison and `reverse_direction_is_active` are what fail.

Flip the SIGN of the mechanical -> thermal term, so expanding the body heats it instead of cooling it. At a real metal's coupling strength this converges cleanly onto a temperature field wrong by twice the coupling effect — the silent-wrong shape — and only the monolithic comparison sees it. RUN AND CONFIRMED to kill.
